title: Za'atar Roasted Chicken Thighs
seoTitle: Za'atar Roasted Chicken Thighs | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Middle Eastern spice-crusted thighs with roasted onions and lemon
subtitle: Middle Eastern spice-crusted thighs with roasted onions and lemon
description: Chicken thighs roast with za'atar, olive oil, lemon, and red onion until the spice crust is fragrant and skin crisps.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Za'atar Roasted Chicken Thighs in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Mix za'atar oil
steps.instruction: Stir za'atar, olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper until combined into a loose paste that coats the back of a spoon evenly. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Coat chicken and onion
steps.instruction: Pat thighs dry. Rub generously with za'atar oil. Nest among onion slices and garlic on two half-sheets, skin-side up. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Roast until crisp
steps.instruction: Roast at 425°F 35–40 minutes until skin is deep golden, za'atar fragrant, and internal temp hits 165°F at the thickest point. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest with lemon wedges
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes. Tuck lemon wedges on tray for squeezing. Onion should be soft with charred edges; skin should crackle lightly. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Garnish and portion
steps.instruction: Scatter parsley over tray before portioning. Pan juices should smell lemony and herbal, not acrid or burnt. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Make your own za'atar if blend is stale—sumac should taste tart, not dusty.
Pair with simple rice or pita—let the chicken be the star.
Leftover za'atar oil works as salad dressing next day.
leftovers: Slice into wraps with tahini drizzle.
Shred over a grain bowl with pickled onions.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Three-ingredient vibe with serious flavor. Smells incredible when crew walks in the door.
mealPrepNotes: Mix za'atar oil ahead. Marinate thighs 30 minutes if time allows. Station: Skin-side up always—za'atar crust needs exposed skin to toast. Station: Roast on parchment for easy cleanup of stuck spice crust. Station: Serve with extra za'atar oil drizzle at the line for brightness.
